title: Where does the incubator settle?
hook: A heater pushes harder the colder it gets. Does it reach the target?

knows: heat leaks to a cooler room
doesNotKnow: that a heater whose power is proportional to the shortfall leaves a steady shortfall

misconception: A control system returns exactly to the target.
objective: The learner can explain that with heater power = gain x shortfall, heat leaking to a room 5 colder balances heater power at a shortfall of 5 / (1 + gain): 1 at gain 4, shrinking with gain but never zero.

claims.text: A controller whose output is proportional to the error leaves a steady error of d / (1 + g) when a constant disturbance d acts; raising the gain g shrinks it but never to zero.
claims.source: Astrom & Murray, Feedback Systems, ch. 1 and 3 (proportional control and steady-state error).

claims.text: Toy incubator set to 37, room 32, heater power = gain x (37 - temperature), heat leak rate 1 x (temperature - 32): steady temperature is 36 at gain 4 (a gap of 1), 36.5 at gain 9 (0.5), 36.75 at gain 19 (0.25), and 32 with no heater.
claims.source: Steady state: (32 - T) + g (37 - T) = 0 gives T = (32 + 37g) / (1 + g). Demo.tsx draws the Euler run (dt 0.02, 250 steps) and the node check agrees: 32.000, 36.000, 36.500, 36.750.

claims.text: Model (stated on the stage and in the reveal): a toy incubator with one loop and no delay, starting at room temperature.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #45. Real body temperature control uses more than proportional control (integral-like and feed-forward elements).

recall.question: A heater adds power in proportion to how far the temperature is below the target. The room is colder than the target. Where does it settle?
recall.why: The heater only works while there is a gap, so a gap remains. A higher gain makes it smaller but not zero.
